title: Joe Oliver, Freddie Keppard and other trumpeters compared
summary: He says Oliver made Louis Armstrong but rates Freddie Keppard as good or better, and comments on Baquet, Perez and Louis's lasting success.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh, I pushed a friend of mine. He's the one that made Louis. I guess you know that, don't you? Yeah, he made Louis. And Louis admits that too. He made Louis. That's a lovely player too, Joe Oliver was. He used to call him King Oliver, you know. But I never thought, I never see Joe in that light of calling him King. Freddie Kepper played with, played more principle and more ease, I thought, than all those players. Freddie Kepper. Jaws didn't swell. That's a nice thing. And Joe stayed something. That's a nice thing. He stayed in as he played his thing.
Yeah, Joe. Yeah, Joe. Joe played nicely. But I thought Freddie Kepper was one of the best we had in the business. Freddie Kepper.
Did he have as much rhythm as Joe?

Oh yes, I think. In fact, I thought Freddie was as good as all of them. Exactly about it. Besides, he kept Freddie didn't say much, but I thought Freddie was as good as all of them.
